aaa-positive.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus
aaa-positive.note: In this separate transverse scan, compare the darker residual lumen with the gray thrombus within the larger aneurysm sac.
aaa-positive.alt: Transverse ultrasound of an aneurysm with gray mural thrombus above its dark residual lumen.

echo-aortic-stenosis.title: Continuous-wave Doppler from multiple windows · Figure 5
echo-aortic-stenosis.credit: Liam Ring et al. · British Society of Echocardiography
echo-aortic-stenosis.note: Compare the apical five-chamber envelope in E with the higher right parasternal envelope in F. The published values belong to a separate exam.
echo-aortic-stenosis.alt: The multiwindow echocardiography figure includes apical five-chamber and right parasternal continuous-wave Doppler envelopes in panels E and F.

carotid-plaque.title: Proximal internal carotid plaque and Doppler · Figure 1
carotid-plaque.credit: Yi Li, Shuai Zheng, Jinghan Zhang, Fumin Wang, Xinyao Liu and Wen He · AME Publishing Company
carotid-plaque.note: Follow the posterior-wall plaque in A to the color and pulsed-wave Doppler at the narrowed segment in B. This patient had a higher-grade lesion than the modeled case.
carotid-plaque.alt: Four-panel acquired carotid ultrasound figure. Panel A shows right internal carotid plaque. Panel B shows its Doppler sample and waveform.

thyroid-nodule.title: Taller-than-wide thyroid nodule · Figure 9
thyroid-nodule.credit: André Tojal Pires, Amina Muhamad Mota Mustafá and Márcio Olavo Gomes Magalhães
thyroid-nodule.note: Compare the solid, hypoechoic nodule’s taller-than-wide shape in this separate left-lobe example. The modeled nodule is in the right lobe.
thyroid-nodule.alt: Transverse grayscale ultrasound of a solid hypoechoic taller-than-wide nodule in the left thyroid lobe.

abdomen-biliary-stone.title: Nonimpacted gallstones
abdomen-biliary-stone.credit: Justin Bowra et al. (Dr. Darmas) · The POCUS Atlas
abdomen-biliary-stone.note: Follow the bright intraluminal stones and their dark posterior shadows as the acquired scan sweeps through this separate gallbladder.
abdomen-biliary-stone.alt: Acquired gallbladder ultrasound clip with bright intraluminal stones and posterior acoustic shadowing.
abdomen-biliary-stone.posterTransform: Single GIF frame encoded as a JPEG. Attribution and CC BY-NC 4.0 carry over from the clip.

abdomen-renal-obstruction.title: Moderate right hydronephrosis
abdomen-renal-obstruction.credit: Carlo Zamora, DO · Riverside Regional Medical Center · The POCUS Atlas
abdomen-renal-obstruction.note: Follow the connected dark spaces in the collecting system as the probe fans through this separate right kidney. CT confirmed a stone in the source case.
abdomen-renal-obstruction.alt: Acquired right renal ultrasound clip showing fluid distending the renal collecting system.
abdomen-renal-obstruction.posterTransform: Single GIF frame encoded as a JPEG. Attribution and CC BY-NC 4.0 carry over from the clip.

breast-retroareolar-cyst.title: Simple cyst behind the right nipple · Figure 9A
breast-retroareolar-cyst.credit: Romuald Ferré, Martine Paré, Lisa Smith, Mélanie Thériault, Ann Aldis, Ellen Kao and Benoit Mesurolle
breast-retroareolar-cyst.note: Find the small dark simple cyst in upper panel A. Lower panel B shows a different finding in the contralateral breast of the published patient.
breast-retroareolar-cyst.alt: The upper panel shows a right retroareolar simple cyst. The lower panel shows a separate irregular left retroareolar mass.

breast-axillary-node.title: Axillary lymph node morphology · Figure 1
breast-axillary-node.credit: Jung Min Chang et al. · Korean Breast Cancer Society
breast-axillary-node.note: Compare the thin cortex in the acquired normal node in B with focal cortical thickening in C and loss of the fatty hilum in D. Panel A illustrates caliper placement.
breast-axillary-node.alt: A caliper schematic and three acquired axillary-node scans showing increasing degrees of abnormal morphology.

pregnancy-early-abnormal.title: Right adnexal ectopic pregnancy · Figure 13
pregnancy-early-abnormal.credit: Venkatesh A. Murugan, Bryan O’Sullivan Murphy, Carolyn Dupuis, Alan Goldstein and Young H. Kim · Korean Society of Ultrasound in Medicine
pregnancy-early-abnormal.note: Compare the empty uterine cavity in A with the separate right adnexal sac and embryo in B. Panel C records cardiac activity in the published exam.
pregnancy-early-abnormal.alt: Three transvaginal ultrasound panels showing an empty uterine cavity, a right adnexal sac containing an embryo, and an M-mode heart-rate trace.

pregnancy-first-abnormal.title: Increased nuchal translucency · Figure 2E
pregnancy-first-abnormal.credit: Maciej Korniluk, Andrzej Korniluk and Grzegorz Szewczyk
pregnancy-first-abnormal.note: Compare the calipers spanning the dark space behind the fetal neck. The published scan measures 4.06 mm in a separate pregnancy. Cropped from Figure 2.
pregnancy-first-abnormal.alt: Midsagittal fetal ultrasound with calipers across the nuchal translucency and the annotation NT 4.06 mm.

pregnancy-mid-abnormal.title: Fetal omphalocele · Figure 1
pregnancy-mid-abnormal.credit: Prajwal Dahal, Rudra Prasad Upadhyaya, Ongden Yonjen Tamang and Sabina Parajuli
pregnancy-mid-abnormal.note: Panel B marks bowel herniating through a midline abdominal wall defect in one fetus of a separate twin pregnancy.
pregnancy-mid-abnormal.alt: Four ultrasound panels from a twin pregnancy. A red arrow identifies the abdominal wall herniation in panel B.

pregnancy-late-abnormal.title: Umbilical artery absent end-diastolic flow · Figure 7B
pregnancy-late-abnormal.credit: Kasemsri Srisupundit, Suchaya Luewan and Theera Tongsong
pregnancy-late-abnormal.note: In panel B, follow each umbilical artery envelope back to the baseline before the next beat. A shows low forward flow and C shows reversal in the same published progression.
pregnancy-late-abnormal.alt: Six acquired fetal ultrasound panels. In panel B, the umbilical artery waveform returns to the baseline during diastole.
